lessons.title: Why time matters and how you use it
lessons.html:
Time is precious

Everyone has 24 hours in a day. Some people get much done; others always feel rushed. The difference is often how they plan their time.

In a stable yard time is very important. Horses must be fed at the same times every day. A horse that is fed late can get stressed and is more at risk of colic. Racehorses must be ready for the track at a set time. The farrier and vet come at booked times.

Where does your time go?

Think about a normal day. Write down what you do and how long it takes:

TimeActivity
05:00 - 05:30Get up, wash, eat
05:30 - 06:00Walk to the yard
06:00 - 07:00Feed and water, check horses
07:00 - 09:00Muck out stables
09:00 - 09:30Breakfast break
09:30 - 12:00Grooming, exercise, cleaning tack

This shows you where your time goes. You may find time that is wasted, such as long chats or looking for lost tools.

Time wasters

  • Not knowing what to do next
  • Looking for tools that were not put back
  • Too much time on the phone
  • Doing a job badly and having to do it again
  • Arriving late

Being on time

Being punctual shows respect for your employer, your co-workers and the horses. If you are going to be late, tell your supervisor as early as you can. Know your transport times. Plan to arrive a few minutes early.

Your time outside work matters too: rest, family, church, sport and study. A good plan leaves time for all of these.

lessons.title: Planning your day and week
lessons.html:
Make a to-do list

Each morning, or the night before, write down what you must do. Cross off each job when it is done. This feels good and helps you remember.

Decide what comes first

Not all jobs are equally important. Sort them:

PriorityMeaningExample
1. Urgent and importantDo nowA horse is cast in its stable; feeding time
2. Important, not urgentPlan a time for itClean and oil the saddles; study for your course
3. Urgent, less importantDo quickly or ask for helpAnswering a phone call about a delivery
4. Not urgent, not importantDo later or leaveChatting on social media

Animal welfare and safety always come first.

Use a timetable

A weekly plan helps you see the whole week: farrier on Tuesday, deep clean stables Wednesday, payday Friday, study on Sunday afternoon. Write it on a calendar or in a small notebook.

Set goals

A goal is something you want to reach. Make it clear and give it a date. "By the end of the month I will be able to plait a mane." Then plan small steps: practise 15 minutes each day after lunch.

Tips to save time

  • Get all tools ready before you start a job.
  • Put tools back in the same place every time.
  • Do one job properly so you do not have to do it twice.
  • Do similar jobs together, for example fill all water buckets in one round.
  • Ask for help when you are behind, before it is too late.

When plans change

On a farm plans often change: a horse gets sick, it rains, a truck arrives early. Stay calm. Look at your list again. Decide what is most important now. Tell your supervisor if something will not get done.

Check your plan

At the end of the week look back: Did I do what I planned? What took longer? What can I do better next week?

Key points

  • Know where your time goes and cut out time wasters.
  • Be punctual and tell your supervisor early if you will be late.
  • Make a to-do list and do urgent and important jobs first.
  • Animal welfare and safety always come first.
  • Set clear goals with dates and check your plan each week.
